Resolves #19192

`Collection#findBy` and `Store#forEach` no longer copy all items on every iteration.

The `items` getter returns a copy of the whole array on every read. `findBy` read it inside its loop, and `forEach` passed it to every callback, so both were quadratic.
- **`findBy`** now reads the backing `_items`, re-read on every iteration, so the collection's current state stays visible to the callback.
- **`forEach`** shares one defensive copy across its callbacks, as the third argument of `fn(record, index, items)`:
  - every entry the loop has reached is its Record, so `items[index] === record` holds under lazy hydration as it did on `dev`;
  - the copy is refreshed when a callback changes the store's count;
  - the one change from `dev` is that the copy is now shared across calls, so it is documented as read-only.

The #19192 Contract Ledger records that contract.

Evidence: L1 (unit + timing probe) → L1 required.

agent-preflight: not hosted here; the CI baseline jobs ran.

## AC Evidence
| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | CI: `MassiveData.spec.mjs` "findBy and forEach do not copy the items per iteration" counts reads through the real getter. `findBy` reads it 0 times and `forEach` once per call; on `dev`, `findBy` read it 110 times over 100 items. `Store.spec.mjs` "forEach callback items" holds three contract cases: every reached entry is the Record passed; mutating the copy leaves the store untouched; a record a callback adds is visited and appears in the next copy. |
| AC-2 | 50k timing (Test Evidence): `findBy` 1,802 → 2.5 ms. `forEach` 1,876 → 27 ms eager, against a 16 ms plain `getAt` loop; lazy mode 178 ms against 185 ms. |
| AC-3 | The full unit suite runs in CI. Local run at `45eebec246`: 4,552 passed, 2 skipped. |

## Deltas from ticket
`forEach` keeps `dev`'s hydration and membership behavior in its shared copy, so it is not a plain start-of-loop snapshot as the ticket first proposed. The ledger on #19192 records why.

## Test Evidence
Unit probe, not committed, run with a no-op callback:

```
n = 50,000             dev          this PR     plain getAt loop, fresh store
Collection#findBy      1,802 ms     2.5 ms      —
Store#forEach, eager   1,876 ms     27 ms       16 ms
Store#forEach, lazy    —            178 ms      185 ms (both dominated by record creation)
```

**Discrimination.** The three `Store.spec` contract cases pass on `dev`'s `forEach`, and all three fail on the plain one-copy version at `91c6484dc6`. The getter-count case fails on `dev`'s `findBy` (110 reads).

**Correction** (per the review's R2): the callback argument is the third, not the fourth. The "4,548" I quoted earlier was a local run; the CI unit job at `91c6484dc6` reported 4,515 passed and 36 skipped.
